reason: The text fragment (Exodus 16) describes Yahweh providing manna and establishing the Sabbath law. While the passage depicts the people's disobedience (going out to gather manna on the Sabbath despite having been given enough for two days), it contains no expression of the people blaming their leaders or Yahweh for putting them at risk. The only explicit statement of blame/frustration is Yahweh's directed at the people: 'How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?' The focus is on the people's failure to obey, not on their attribution of blame to leaders or Yahweh.
